response.sql: WITH pairs AS (SELECT f.orderslink, u.acctscope, AVG(f.feerate) AS avg_feerate FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault JOIN users u ON o.userlink = u.userstamp GROUP BY f.orderslink, u.acctscope), m AS (SELECT AVG(avg_feerate) AS mean_avg FROM pairs), kept AS (SELECT p.orderslink, p.acctscope, p.avg_feerate, p.avg_feerate - m.mean_avg AS excess FROM pairs p CROSS JOIN m WHERE p.avg_feerate > m.mean_avg), ranked AS (SELECT orderslink, acctscope, avg_feerate, excess, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY acctscope ORDER BY excess DESC) AS rnk FROM kept) SELECT orderslink, acctscope, avg_feerate, excess, rnk AS rank FROM ranked WHERE rnk <= 3 ORDER BY acctscope, rnk, orderslink

assumptions.assumption: The mean of all pair averages is the unweighted mean across (orderslink, acctscope) pairs, taken before filtering. Pairs whose feerate values are all NULL have a NULL average and are excluded from that mean and from the kept set.

Inner joins implement the drop-unmatched rule. If users.userstamp is not unique, a fee could be matched to more than one user and its row duplicated. The request treats userstamp as a key, so I did not deduplicate.
